caption: Hebrews explicitly gives Psalm 22:22 to Jesus, and John shows the risen Jesus addressing his brothers. Strong typology—but the verse never states resurrection.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Psalm 22 predict Jesus’s resurrection? The rescued psalmist promises to speak to his brothers. John shows the risen Jesus sending a message to his brothers.
slides.body: The rescued psalmist promises to speak to his brothers. John shows the risen Jesus sending a message to his brothers.
slides.heading: Did Psalm 22 predict Jesus’s resurrection?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ps 22:22: I will proclaim Your name to my brothers.
slides.body: I will proclaim Your name to my brothers.
slides.heading: Ps 22:22

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Jn 20:17, BSB: “ Do not cling to Me,” Jesus said, “for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go and tell My brothers, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.’”
slides.body: “ Do not cling to Me,” Jesus said, “for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go and tell My brothers, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.’”
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Jn 20:17

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: The Christian link is strong Hebrews directly quotes this verse as Jesus’s words. Psalm 22 also turns here from suffering to praise.

slides.heading: The Christian link is strong

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But resurrection is not stated The speaker has been rescued and will praise God. The verse never says he died and returned to life.

title: The risen Jesus and his brothers
